motion: Is religious disagreement evidence against God’s existence?

bridges.description: Show that the observed degree and distribution of fundamental religious disagreement are more expected if God does not exist than if God exists.
Establish that a truth-valuing relational God would have reason to correct consequential false beliefs that impair willing, informed relationship.
Distinguish generic supernatural belief from independently convergent detailed doctrine and explain why the latter counterfactual sharpens the evidential comparison.
Show that agreement or disagreement alone underdetermines theism versus atheism, so the observed disagreement need not support atheism.
Identify coherent divine reasons for permitting disagreement, including formation, staged teaching, freedom and accommodation, that weaken the proposed expectation.
Show that relationship and fair judgment need not require uniform detailed doctrine because acquaintance, general moral awareness and response to available evidence can matter.

sections.title: From fundamental disagreement to evidence
sections.rationale: Defines the phenomenon, its claimed relational tension and the comparative burden at the center of the motion.

sections.title: Possible reasons to permit disagreement
sections.rationale: Tests whether formation, freedom, accommodation and fair judgment make the observed disagreement compatible with divine purposes.

sections.title: Truth, salvation and kinds of relationship
sections.rationale: Addresses whether doctrinal error matters independently of exclusivism and whether acquaintance can substitute for informed mutual relationship.

sections.title: Independent doctrinal convergence
sections.rationale: Compares explanations of broad belief and detailed doctrine while preserving the distinction between possible convergence and actual evidential support.

sections.title: Closing scope and cumulative force
sections.rationale: Records the defeasible scope of the pro case and the con side’s final treatment of continuing intra-Christian disagreement.

moves.speaker: Justin Schieber
moves.claim: Fundamental incompatible beliefs among devout believers create tension among believers and between believers and God.
moves.warrant: In the landlord analogy, conflicting private-message claims about identity and obligations frustrate clarity and relationships; religious believers likewise report incompatible revelation claims about central matters.
moves.inference: A relational God’s apparent failure to prevent or correct fundamental confusion is evidence calling for explanation.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Begins after the mixed host fragment with Schieber’s analogy and ends after he distinguishes fundamental religious questions from trivial disputes.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: these kind of disagreements introduce tension that wouldn't otherwise be there
the kind of disagreement I'm interested in is the kind of disagreement that's very fundamental
moves.attributionRationale: The host hands the floor to Schieber, who introduces his own book analogy and continues in first person throughout the selected argument.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed for ownership; the named handoff and sustained first-person continuity are clear in the captions.
moves.importanceRationale: This supplies the core phenomenon and divine expectation from which the pro motion case begins.

burdenContact.rationale: It specifies how fundamental disagreement allegedly damages the relationship a relational God would seek.

moves.speaker: Randal Rauser
moves.claim: The landlord analogy need not carry over, and Schieber must show why the actual degree of disagreement is beyond what God could permissibly allow.
moves.warrant: A theist may hold that God revealed information to one group and not another rather than issued contradictions, and Schieber already allows that some differential revelation can have sufficient reasons.
moves.inference: Observed disagreement is not by itself a sustainable objection unless its amount and distribution are shown to be evidentially unacceptable.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Covers Rauser’s complete initial response: his challenge to the analogy’s revelation assumption and his linked burden concerning degree and distribution.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the burden of proof is then on him
he has to explain why the degree of disagreement we do in fact find
moves.attributionRationale: The host explicitly asks Randal for his response, and the answer uses third-person references to Justin while advancing Rauser’s position.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed because the named handoff and argumentative continuity make ownership clear.
moves.importanceRationale: This is the con side’s primary challenge to the inference from disagreement to evidence against God.

burdenContact.rationale: It argues that the raw fact and degree of disagreement do not yet discriminate between theism and atheism.

responseComponents.description: Challenges the analogy’s assumption about divine communication and demands an account of why the actual degree is excessive.

moves.speaker: Justin Schieber
moves.claim: The issue is not that God gives incompatible revelations but that fundamental claimed revelations conflict and a relational God has reasons to correct the resulting misunderstandings.
moves.warrant: The disputes concern salvation, divine nature, history and moral-political requirements, rather than low-stakes matters where self-resolution plausibly builds character.
moves.inference: The seriousness of the errors makes nonintervention harder to explain under theism even without attributing contradictions directly to God.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Includes Schieber’s toddler contrast, catalogue of fundamental disputes, express denial of contradictory divine revelation, and reason for corrective clarification.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I'm not making that claim
God has reasons to correct those misunderstandings
moves.attributionRationale: Although the preceding question addresses Rauser, first-person reference to Schieber’s argument, the toddler example, and the later handoff back to Randal establish Schieber as speaker.
moves.audioVerificationReason: The source notes expressly resolve this potentially confusing handoff through first-person continuity; no further audio check is required.
moves.importanceRationale: It preserves a crucial qualification and answers the central misreading of the pro argument.

burdenContact.rationale: It connects consequential error to reasons a truth-valuing relational God would have to clarify matters.

responseComponents.description: Rejects the premise that the argument attributes contradictory revelations to God and specifies why the relevant degree matters.

moves.speaker: Randal Rauser
moves.claim: Disagreement may serve virtue formation and staged divine teaching.
moves.warrant: A team-building task develops character through interpretive tension, while a teacher appropriately gives simplified or differing instruction according to students’ developmental level.
moves.inference: Some religious disagreement can be explained by God’s pedagogical accommodation rather than divine absence.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Starts with Rauser’s answer to the host’s request for reasons and includes both his team-building and grammar-teaching analogies through their conclusion.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: that is all part of building virtues and character
God as a master pedagogue or master teacher
moves.attributionRationale: The host explicitly returns the question to Randal, whose answer supplies examples identified elsewhere in the discussion as his.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed; the named handoff and later references consistently identify these analogies as Rauser’s.
moves.importanceRationale: This supplies concrete sufficient reasons central to the con route rather than merely asserting possibility.

burdenContact.rationale: It offers observable proposed goods—character formation and developmentally fitted instruction—that could justify permitted disagreement.

responseComponents.description: Offers developmental and character-building reasons why immediate uniform correction may not be required.

moves.speaker: Randal Rauser
moves.claim: Freedom, general moral knowledge and judgment proportionate to available revelation can mitigate the stakes of religious disagreement.
moves.warrant: Rauser cites value in freely seeking God, a moral law written on human hearts, and the principle that people are judged according to the revelation accessible to them.
moves.inference: Lack of uniform detailed doctrine need not entail unfair divine treatment or the loss of all relevant guidance.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Excludes the initial mixed host words, then captures Rauser’s three stated reasons and his conclusion about judgment based on accessible revelation.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: God judges each person appropriately based upon the degree of Revelation
he doesn't force himself upon us
moves.attributionRationale: After the mixed event’s host fragment, Rauser says he likes the setup and enumerates his own three points.
moves.audioVerificationReason: The mixed boundary is explicitly documented and the scored words begin only with Rauser’s response, so no audio verification is needed.
moves.importanceRationale: It directly addresses alleged relational and salvific harm with an alternative account of responsibility.

burdenContact.rationale: It gives criteria for fair judgment and meaningful guidance despite unequal doctrinal access.

responseComponents.description: Argues that consequences of error are mitigated when judgment tracks accessible knowledge and general moral awareness.

moves.speaker: Justin Schieber
moves.claim: The team-building analogy supports Schieber because radically different understandings of the task prevent successful cooperation.
moves.warrant: A team cannot combine strengths when each member has different problems, rules and deadlines; an instructor would be expected to clarify the shared goal from the top down.
moves.inference: Fundamental religious disagreement defeats the proposed team-building good unless God provides the clarity that appears absent.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Captures Schieber’s complete reconstruction of the team-building analogy and the resulting demand for top-down clarification.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: that's the exact argument that I'm forwarding
we do not have that top-down clarification
moves.attributionRationale: The host asks Justin directly, and Schieber explicitly names and reconstructs Randal’s team-building analogy.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed because the direct handoff and named target make ownership clear.
moves.importanceRationale: This is the principal pro answer to the con side’s character-building rationale.

burdenContact.rationale: It argues that the kind of disagreement observed blocks rather than advances the relational cooperation offered as justification.

responseComponents.description: Refashions the team exercise to show that disagreement over the task itself prevents its proposed benefits.

moves.speaker: Randal Rauser
moves.claim: Religious disagreement can arise from human mistake or rebellion, while accommodation and a cross-cultural moral framework preserve shared guidance.
moves.warrant: God need not reveal contradictory specifics; a manager may tailor information to differing aptitudes, and Rauser’s appeal to moral law supplies common obligations across cultures.
moves.inference: Schieber’s team reconstruction does not establish that God caused the conflict or withheld every common rule.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Begins with Rauser’s explicit return to Schieber’s refashioned analogy and includes all three numbered responses through his stated conclusion.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: some religious disagreement is simply the result of people being mistaken
provide a framework that transcends cultures
moves.attributionRationale: The host names Randal, and Rauser refers to Justin’s rebuttal while numbering his own responses.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed because the handoff and response structure clearly establish the speaker.
moves.importanceRationale: It combines the con side’s direct causal correction with its positive account of shared guidance.

burdenContact.rationale: It supplies accommodation and human error as alternatives to the claim that God generates or inexplicably tolerates confusion.

responseComponents.description: Denies that the actual case has an instructor giving incompatible tasks and identifies a common moral framework.
Reiterates that conflicting claims may reflect human mistake or rebellion rather than contradictory divine communication.

moves.speaker: Justin Schieber
moves.claim: Schieber’s analogy concerns incompatible beliefs sincerely taken as revelation, not God actually issuing incompatible revelations.
moves.warrant: When team members hold fundamentally different views of the goal, cooperation fails and the instructor would be expected to clarify even if the instructor did not cause each belief.
moves.inference: Human misinterpretation does not remove the evidential problem of absent correction.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Starts after the host’s independent prevalence argument and includes Schieber’s renewed qualification plus his complete explanation of the team goal problem.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I'm not advocating that God is somehow giving incompatible revelations
you would expect the instructor at that point to clarify the goal
moves.attributionRationale: The host’s question ends before the selected span; Schieber then speaks in first person about the argument and its analogy.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed because the first-person clarification and subsequent analogy continuation identify Schieber.
moves.importanceRationale: It prevents a repeated misconstrual from displacing the actual pro burden.

burdenContact.rationale: It maintains that correction is expected even when God is not the source of the false beliefs.

responseComponents.description: Accepts that God need not cause incompatible beliefs but argues that an instructor still should clarify fundamental error.

moves.speaker: Randal Rauser
moves.claim: Religious relationship can involve valuable acquaintance knowledge before or without detailed propositional doctrine.
moves.warrant: An infant has a developing acquaintance with a parent before learning propositions about that parent, showing that relational depth is not exhausted by doctrinal accuracy.
moves.inference: Doctrinal disagreement alone may overstate how deficient divine-human relationship is.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Follows the host’s question and covers Rauser’s full distinction between propositional and acquaintance knowledge through its application to the objection.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: there is also a knowledge of acquaintance or a knowledge of experience
all the time they have an acquaintance knowledge of their parent
moves.attributionRationale: The host asks Randal by name, and the reply directly contrasts Justin’s focus with Rauser’s relational distinction.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed; the direct address and sustained response are unambiguous.
moves.importanceRationale: This introduces a distinct model of relationship that directly contests the pro expectation of doctrinal clarity.

burdenContact.rationale: It identifies acquaintance as a form of relationship whose presence is not measured by doctrinal uniformity.

responseComponents.description: Argues that clarification of propositions is not the sole measure of divine-human relational success.

moves.speaker: Justin Schieber
moves.claim: A freely chosen relationship in which both parties are aware is more meaningful than a relationship lacking mutual awareness.
moves.warrant: Relationships operate as two-way streets and are best when willing, aware participants enter them; Schieber grants a substantive lesser relationship but asks why God would settle for it.
moves.inference: Acquaintance without accurate awareness does not fully answer why God permits false understandings that obstruct richer relationship.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Begins with Schieber’s direct answer, includes his concession of some substantive relationship, and ends with his challenge concerning a vaguer relationship.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: relationships are going to be two-way streets
the most meaningful relationships are those which are entered into by free
moves.attributionRationale: The host yields to Justin, who answers in first person and explicitly discusses the distinction raised with Randal in their book.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed because the handoff and first-person response clearly identify Schieber.
moves.importanceRationale: It preserves the pro concession while explaining why acquaintance does not exhaust the relational expectation.

burdenContact.rationale: It states the richer relational outcome that uniform or corrected understanding would facilitate.

responseComponents.description: Grants some acquaintance value but argues that willing mutual awareness is relationally richer and remains unexplained.

moves.speaker: Justin Schieber
moves.claim: Independent convergence on specific doctrines would strongly favor theism, whereas the actual widespread disagreement favors atheism comparatively.
moves.warrant: Generic supernatural belief may have evolutionary explanations, but matching detailed doctrines across unconnected populations would be difficult for atheism and readily explained by revelation.
moves.inference: The contrast between that counterfactual and the actual world gives disagreement evidential force against God.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Starts with Schieber’s explicit abductive framing and includes the full independent-continent counterfactual through his comparative conclusion.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: its inductive it's well it probably better posed as an abductor of argument
the disagreement that we have in our actual world is evidence against God
moves.attributionRationale: After the host’s summary, Schieber explicitly characterizes the argument and presents his own counterfactual.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed; the first-person formulation and direct continuation identify Schieber.
moves.importanceRationale: This is the clearest statement of the motion as defeasible comparative evidence rather than deduction.

burdenContact.rationale: It directly states how the actual observation is claimed to discriminate between the rival worldviews.

moves.speaker: Randal Rauser
moves.claim: Agreement could arise through undirected convergent pressures, so agreement and disagreement alone underdetermine theism versus atheism.
moves.warrant: Rauser compares independently recurring biological structures and proposes that selection could likewise produce broad theological agreement without intelligence.
moves.inference: Neither higher agreement nor present disagreement automatically supplies a reliable argument for or against God.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Begins with Rauser’s explicit denial that he would infer God from convergence and includes his biological analogy and underdetermination conclusion, stopping before break language.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I simply disagree I wouldn't do that
that really under determines the question of theism versus atheism
moves.attributionRationale: Rauser answers the convergence challenge in first person; the following host interjection is excluded from the selected ending.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed because first-person continuity and the documented break boundary identify the selected words.
moves.importanceRationale: It directly contests the comparative premise connecting the counterfactual to the actual evidential conclusion.

burdenContact.rationale: It argues that either agreement pattern may have a natural explanation and therefore does not settle the evidential comparison.

responseComponents.description: Rejects the claim that independent agreement would uniquely favor revelation by proposing convergent natural processes.

moves.speaker: Justin Schieber
moves.claim: Natural explanations for generic spirit belief do not plausibly extend to independent agreement on content-rich doctrines.
moves.warrant: Schieber distinguishes broad supernatural-person concepts from doctrines such as a triune God, divine simplicity and particular atonement theories, for which no plausible selective pressure is identified.
moves.inference: Because detailed agreement would favor God, widespread detailed disagreement supplies comparative evidence against God.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Excludes the mixed opening host fragment, then captures Schieber’s complete closing distinction between generic belief and named detailed doctrines through his inference.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the specificity ends starkly
doctrinal disagreement in to the widespread degree that we have it
moves.attributionRationale: The mixed initial host words are excluded from the claim; Schieber begins with 'sure so' and develops his own earlier convergence argument.
moves.audioVerificationReason: The boundary is documented in the source notes and the subsequent first-person argument clearly belongs to Schieber.
moves.importanceRationale: This is the required specific-doctrine answer to the con natural-convergence proposal.

burdenContact.rationale: It supplies the observable distinction between generic belief and detailed independent doctrinal convergence.

responseComponents.description: Limits plausible evolutionary convergence to general belief and challenges its extension to detailed independent doctrines.

moves.speaker: Randal Rauser
moves.claim: Even if greater agreement supported God, it would not follow that the current relative lack of agreement supports atheism.
moves.warrant: Evidence at one end of a comparison need not make the actual alternative evidence for the negation, and broad naturalistic accounts already explain some cross-cultural agreement.
moves.inference: Schieber’s counterfactual does not by itself establish the directional evidential claim about the actual world.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Includes Rauser’s projection-theory response for broad convergence and preserves his distinct final logical point through the host’s next turn.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: even if agreement did support God
it doesn't follow that the state of affairs we are currently in supports atheism
moves.attributionRationale: The host asks Randal to reply, and Rauser distinguishes the two Justins while making his own concluding points.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed; the named handoff and explicit wrap-up identify Rauser.
moves.importanceRationale: The contract requires this closing inference to remain distinct from the earlier possibility of natural convergence.

burdenContact.rationale: It directly denies that the counterfactual evidential relation determines the evidential sign of current disagreement.

responseComponents.description: Answers the specificity-based closing inference by denying that hypothetical support fixes actual-world support.
Separates the evidential status of greater agreement from the status of present disagreement.

moves.speaker: Justin Schieber
moves.claim: The disagreement argument has significant but defeasible weight within a cumulative comparison of theism and atheism.
moves.warrant: Other theistic arguments may outweigh disagreement and other atheistic arguments; the disagreement case is not a deductive demonstration that belief in God is irrational.
moves.inference: The proper conclusion is a serious evidential contribution against God, not a conclusive disproof.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Begins with Schieber’s answer about strength and includes his allowance for outweighing theistic arguments plus his express rejection of deductive conclusiveness.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: this is is but one argument among many
this is certainly not a deductive argument
moves.attributionRationale: The host asks Justin how strong the argument is, and Schieber answers in first person about its role among other arguments.
moves.audioVerificationReason: No audio verification is needed because the direct question and self-characterization make ownership clear.
moves.importanceRationale: This qualification fixes the intended burden and prevents the inventory from turning the case into a deductive claim.

burdenContact.rationale: It defines success as adding comparative evidential weight while permitting contrary cumulative evidence.

moves.speaker: Randal Rauser
moves.claim: Continuing Christian disagreement is serious, but God may have sufficient reasons to permit it because charitable debate and ecumenical engagement realize relational goods.
moves.warrant: Rauser acknowledges disputes over baptism and ordinances, proposes providential ambiguity in debates such as Calvinism and Arminianism, and cites improved fellowship and the value of listening across traditions.
moves.inference: The acknowledged internal disagreement does not sustain the atheistic inference when it can serve relational development.
moves.sourceSpanSelectionRationale: Starts with Rauser’s express acknowledgment that the argument should not be brushed away and runs through his final claimed relational value, excluding the host’s closing word.
quoteEligibleExactSpans: this is something we have to take seriously

moves.audioVerificationReason: The source notes explicitly set the final boundary before the host’s 'it’s'; the selected argumentative voice is Rauser’s.
moves.importanceRationale: It is the con side’s final concession and application to the strongest internal-disagreement example.

burdenContact.rationale: It acknowledges the data while identifying charitable inquiry and fellowship as sufficient relational goods.

responseComponents.description: Accepts that the concern deserves serious consideration but maintains that sufficient reasons and realized goods prevent it from sustaining the motion.
